subject: Clarify roles & breach notification timeline for DPA — follow-up
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Steele <hannah@finbanktech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify roles & breach notification timeline for DPA — follow-up

Hi Hannah / Oliver —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the follow-up items we promised:

1) Roles (controller vs. processor): you asked us to confirm how Redwood sees the relationship for the features you plan to use (inference + optional logging for telemetry). At a high level Redwood would be the processor for the inference endpoints; FinBank Technologies would be the controller for the customer data you send in, except for telemetry logs where you can opt-in to sharing aggregated logs for performance insights.

2) Subprocessors: I attached the current subprocessors list (redwood_subprocessors_20260224.csv). Please note that our list is updated quarterly. We will provide notice of new subprocessors per the DPA clause we discussed.

3) Breach notification: you asked whether we can commit to a specific notification timeline. Our standard DPA language is "without undue delay" with an update cadence during investigation. You requested a clearer SLA (e.g., initial notification within 24–48 hours and detailed report within 72 hours). I’ve looped in Rishi and Mina from Security/Privacy to confirm feasibility and any constraints.

4) Data residency & retention: you requested EU-only residency for production logs and PII. We can offer EU-only residency for customer data on Dedicated or Private deployments — we flagged this as a configuration requirement for your procurement team.

Deliverables attached: Redwood_DPA_Summary_v1.pdf (high-level answers + proposed edits) and the subprocessors CSV.

Next steps (proposed):
- Rishi: confirm proposed breach-notification language and whether we can commit to an initial notice within 24 hours + follow-up within 72 hours.
- Mina: confirm logging controls (who can access audit logs, retention defaults, encryption at rest/in transit).
- Lauren: propose contract timeline and route for EU-only deployment option.

Can we aim to have an updated DPA mark-up by EOD Wednesday?

Thanks —

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.ai
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_Summary_v1.pdf (PDF), redwood_subprocessors_20260224.csv (CSV)

From: Hannah Steele <hannah@finbanktech.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finbanktech.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 13:38:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Clarify roles & breach notification timeline for DPA — follow-up

Hi Lauren —

Thanks for the clear recap — that is helpful. A few clarifying questions from our legal and security teams after reviewing the summary:

- Controller/processor: Can Redwood explicitly state in the DPA that any telemetry logs we opt into are processed as "pseudonymized operational telemetry" and will not be used for model training? We need this in writing for our internal auditors.

- Subprocessors: If Redwood adds a new subprocessor, is there a notification window (we'd prefer 30 days) and a right to object for critical services?

- Breach notice SLA: Our security team will be satisfied with an initial informational notification within 24 hours of detection and a substantive update within 72 hours. If your investigation needs more time for remediation detail, we expect frequent updates. Can you confirm Redwood will accept that timeline?

- Data retention: We have a hard limit of 90 days for PII in logging for this pilot. Is that configurable per account?

Please copy your security/privacy folks on the answers so we can close these items in the procurement checklist.

Regards,
Hannah Steele
Head of Platform Security | FinBank Technologies
Hannah.Steele@finbanktech.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Steele <hannah@finbanktech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 07:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify roles & breach notification timeline for DPA — follow-up

Hannah —

Thanks for the questions. Quick answers and proposed contract language snippets below. Keeping it pragmatic to move the deal forward while protecting both parties.

1) Telemetry and training
Proposed language (for DPA / Addendum): "Redwood will treat telemetry data as operational telemetry and will not use such telemetry for model training, tuning, or benchmarking without Customer's prior written consent. Telemetry may be processed for operational purposes (performance, reliability, and capacity planning) and will be pseudonymized where feasible."

2) Subprocessor notifications
We can commit to a 30-day notice window for new subprocessors with an exception process for emergency additions (e.g., short-lived cloud provider changes). Proposed language: "Redwood will provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days' prior written notice of the addition of a new subprocessor and will provide a reasonable opportunity to object on legitimate data-protection grounds."

3) Breach notification timeline
Our internal detection/investigation cadence varies by incident. Operationally we can do the following: initial notification within 24 hours of confirmed detection (or sooner for high-confidence incidents), then a detailed incident report within 72 hours that contains scope, mitigations taken, and next steps where possible. We prefer to avoid a hard commitment to full remediation within 72 hours because root-cause and remediation timelines can extend. Proposed DPA text: "Redwood will notify Customer of a Security Incident affecting Customer Data without undue delay and, to the extent feasible, within twenty-four (24) hours of discovery. Redwood will provide a substantive written update within seventy-two (72) hours describing known scope and mitigations and will continue to provide regular updates until the incident is resolved."

4) Retention controls
Yes — retention for PII in logs is configurable at the account level. For the pilot we can set a default of 90 days and we will document the configuration steps. Access to raw logs is restricted to personnel with explicit role-based access; audit logs record access events and are retained for 12 months by default (we can provide exportable audit records for your audits).

I'm attaching a short DPA snippet and the subprocessors list for reference (see attachments Lauren shared). If that language works, Lauren — can you send this as a proposed mark-up to FinBank and suggest we run DocuSign once legal confirms?

-Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security & Privacy | Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.ai

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Steele <hannah@finbanktech.com>, Oliver Grant <oliver.grant@finbanktech.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarify roles & breach notification timeline for DPA — follow-up

Hannah / Oliver —

Great — thanks Rishi and Mina for the quick turnaround. Per Rishi's suggested language we will:

• Add the telemetry clause stating telemetry won't be used for model training without consent.
• Commit to 30-day subprocessor notices with an emergency exception.
• Commit to initial notification within 24 hours of discovery and a substantive update within 72 hours (with continued status updates until resolution).
• Configure account-level log retention to 90 days for PII for the pilot; audit logs retained 12 months and exportable on request.

Next steps:
- I will send a DPA mark-up PDF and a DocuSign packet by EOD today.
- Rishi / Mina, please confirm you are happy for me to include the quoted snippets as-is in the DPA mark-up.

Hannah — if you can review the mark-up and flag any final redlines, we can aim to have signatures within the week and spin up EU-residency for your pilot environment during onboarding.

Thanks all —

Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren@redwood.ai
